problem: Consider the arc of the curve $x=\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}$ that lies between the lines $y=0$ and $y=\sqrt[4]{3}.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.

activity_context.topic_title: Surface Areas of Revolution: Rotation About the Y-Axis

feedback.problem: Consider the arc of the curve $y={(4-{x}^{2/3})}^{3/2}$ that lies between the lines $x=0$ and $x=1.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $y=f(x),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{(4-{x}^{2/3})}^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{(4-{x}^{2/3})}^{1/2}(-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{-1/3}) \\  & =-{x}^{-1/3}{(4-{x}^{2/3})}^{1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}={x}^{-2/3}(4-{x}^{2/3})=4{x}^{-2/3}-1.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}x\sqrt{1+(4{x}^{-2/3}-1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}x\sqrt{4{x}^{-2/3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot {x}^{-1/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {[\frac{3}{5}{x}^{5/3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{12\pi }{5}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{12\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
